### Exported finite-slew example

The explicit source is

\[
H=X/2,\qquad L=Z,
\]

so

\[
\mathcal L(\rho)
=-i[X/2,\rho]+Z\rho Z-\rho.
\]

It relaxes to \(I/2\). The source remains unchanged during reception. The receiver consists of two qubits initialized in a local Bell state.

For \(\epsilon=0.003\) and \(T=8\), I exported every control coefficient and replayed the resulting program independently on all four input matrix units.

| Quantity | Replayed result |
|---|---:|
| Receiver dimension | \(4\) |
| Continuous linear control segments | \(1{,}026\) |
| Logical entanglement fidelity | \(0.9982347817\) |
| Computed Choi expression bounding full diamond error | \(0.0070650155\) |
| Source-marginal discrepancy | \(4.24\times10^{-16}\) |
| Peak receiver coupling norm | \(35.3180\) |
| Peak receiver Hamiltonian norm | \(9.12506\) |
| Maximum coupling slew | \(7.26186\times10^5\) |
| Shortest control interval | \(9.08\times10^{-7}\) |

All times and control magnitudes use the stated source Markov units. The receiver ports are off at both endpoints. A separately supplied local Hamiltonian implements the final gauge unitary with chosen duration \(1\) and norm \(2.6931237\). Preparation, source loading, propagation, readout and reset remain additional.

The large coupling and slew requirements matter. This example demonstrates a mathematically specified receiver operation; it does not establish that a particular laboratory platform supports the required controls.

The reported diamond expression is computed from the normalized Choi matrix. The replay uses floating-point arithmetic, not interval-certified enclosures, so it is model evidence rather than a certified physical error bar. The illustrative fidelity is also not claimed to meet the conservative threshold used in the general coding proof.

Independent implementations checked generic complex nonunital qutrit sources with nine-level receivers. The principal dark-state, tangent, normalization, gauge and endpoint identities agreed to residuals below \(2.05\times10^{-13}\). Those checks support the implementation and conventions; the universal claims rest on the proofs.
